children: Oil gains in early Asian trade. Stabilizers in the global oil market appear to be weakening with China's crude oil imports edging higher and non-OPEC+ supply outside the Middle East likely to only come online in 2027, says Commonwealth Bank of Australia's Vivek Dhar in a note. Dhar finds it difficult to predict when oil flows in the Strait of Hormuz--through which one-fifth of the world's oil typically passes--will recover materially, given still-elevated U.S.-Iran tensions. CBA's low estimate of global markets having five to 11 weeks of oil and refined product stockpiles is growing more likely, the strategist adds. Front-month WTI crude-oil futures are up 1.3% at $102.69 a barrel, while front-month Brent is 1.3% higher at $107.01 a barrel. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)
